card: Switches getblocktemplate cache age tracking from the system clock to a steady clock. After mempool updates, template rebuilds are throttled to once every 5 seconds, but measuring this with system time makes rebuild timing vulnerable to wall-clock adjustments or steps. The PR also updates unit and functional tests to handle the steady clock, which is unaffected by setmocktime. It addresses review feedback on PR 36356 and depends on PR 36356 and PR 36921.
changed_since_previous: None; this is the first description generated with the diff provided.
evidence: PR description cites review feedback on #36356: 'a steady clock is the better fit for measuring an interval, since system time changes don't affect it', following precedent from #30372.
problem: When mempool transactions change, getblocktemplate throttles template rebuilds by checking whether the cached template is more than 5 seconds old using system time. System wall-clock jumps or NTP adjustments can cause the rebuild interval to trigger prematurely or be delayed.

risk.why: A logic error in the template age check could cause getblocktemplate to rebuild too frequently or delay including new mempool transactions for miners.

scope_notes: Only the final commit is new to this PR; the first four commits are inherited from stacked dependencies #36356 and #36921.
summary: Switches the getblocktemplate template rebuild interval measurement from the system clock to a steady clock. This ensures that the 5-second template caching interval following mempool updates is not disrupted by system clock adjustments. The PR also updates functional and unit tests to accommodate steady clock behavior.
